name: Winds in the Desert
summary: A stolen supply caravan leaves Rezlak waiting in Durotar. Dustwind harpies ambushed it in Razorwind Canyon, scattering the construction materials among the cliffs.

sections.title: A Goblin on a Deadline
sections.body: Rezlak came directly from Ratchet, sent by Chief Engineer Gazlowe to help the Horde build across Durotar. The harsh, barren land already makes fortification work hard. Now shipments keep vanishing before they reach the building sites, and without the cargo, work stops. The irritable goblin supervisor has nothing to build with.

sections.title: Ambush in the Canyon
sections.body: Dustwind harpies ambushed the latest supply run in Razorwind Canyon. They roost along the high ravines beside the road from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar, then swoop on passing wagons. These scavengers do not eat or destroy the freight. They hoard the crates and sacks near their nests, where the supplies remain for anyone willing to fight through their territory.

faq.answer: Rezlak is a goblin worker employed by Gazlowe, the boss of Ratchet. Gazlowe sent him to Durotar to help the orcs with construction outside Orgrimmar's gates.

faq.q: Why are goblins helping build in Durotar?
faq.answer: Gazlowe and the Steamwheedle Cartel have a commercial and engineering partnership with Warchief Thrall. Goblin engineers and machines helped lay Orgrimmar's foundations, and Gazlowe still supplies contracted labor and materials to the Horde.

faq.q: Where did the supplies come from?
faq.answer: Rezlak does not say where the shipment began. He says only that a caravan carried supplies for his work with the orcs in Durotar.

faq.q: What are the harpies doing in Durotar?
faq.answer: Dustwind harpies are aggressive, predatory scavengers that infest the cliffs and ravines of central Durotar. They harass travelers, raid trade along Razorwind Canyon, and gather anything bright or useful for their nests.
Razorwind Canyon branches from the main southern gorge between Orgrimmar and Razor Hill. Ravines cut into both cliff walls, giving Dustwind harpies high roosts where they stash stolen cargo.

faq.q: Why didn't the orc guards protect the caravan?
faq.answer: Rezlak says caravans are hard to keep safe and that this shipment was promised safe passage. He does not say what guards went with it or why they failed to stop the Dustwind harpies.

angles.text: Each shipment lost to canyon beasts threatens the Horde's rapid expansion and the fortification of its stronghold in Durotar.
As an orc, you rely on goblin skill and foreign supplies to make Durotar's harsh, dry soil a fortified homeland.
As an engineer, you can understand why Rezlak prizes sound plans and on-time deliveries, even with local wildlife causing trouble.
